question: For a UK buyer choosing between a new ECM Classika III and a discounted or used Classika PID, is the III’s faster advertised warm-up worth the price premium?
commissionedQuestion: How can a UK shopper tell a Classika III from a Classika PID in a listing, and what should they ask a used PID seller to demonstrate from a cold start?
answer: Ask for a photo of the item number and controls. ECM lists the III as CM100024-00, with an OLED display and rotary dial, and the current PID as CM100003-00. For a used PID, confirm which manual applies to the unit. If it covers the documented Fast Heat-Up sequence, ask for a demonstration starting with the machine cold. At FLU, the seller should flush until the display shows rdY/Go, ECM’s cue to brew the first cup. ECM advertises 6.5 minutes to brew readiness for the III and 11 minutes for the currently listed PID. Those figures give buyers a reason to ask for a demonstration, while the value of the premium remains open.
evidence: ECM’s catalogues establish the model identifiers, controls and advertised readiness figures. ECM attributes the III’s faster advertised warm-up to its heated Core Heat group. The applicable PID manual gives the buyer an observable cue and action: flush at FLU and continue until rdY/Go. The UK listings show both model names in shopping results, and the buyer thread shows that cold-start time mattered to one shopper. Neither establishes the price premium or the time a buyer would save in practice.
missingEvidence: To reopen the premium question, obtain comparable UK purchase prices for an available new III and representative discounted or used PIDs, accounting for condition and warranty. Run repeatable cold-start tests on the III and the PID revisions buyers are likely to encounter, using the same first-shot readiness criterion and including any required flush. Verify the III’s startup procedure and which older PIDs support the documented Fast Heat-Up sequence. If the story also promises a faster milk-drink workflow, measure brew–steam–brew times for both machines.
